html:
SMTO-POL-0018 — A quick data calculation tried to do more than it's allowed

GUID: 3ad050c3-6e4b-4639-a187-0e3e3e9b91b4
Slug: transform-sandbox-guard
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Agent wrote a small data-processing program that tried to open files, run programs, use the network or other off-limits features. These quick calculations may only work on the data they're given, so it didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment to see whether the Agent rewrites the calculation or switches to a different kind of step by itself. SMTO tells the Agent which feature was off-limits, so it can choose an allowed approach.
  2. If the task stops, reply asking the Agent to read the files or data it needs first, then do the calculation on that data. Reading files is a separate step with its own permission checks; the calculation can then use what was read.
  3. If an Approval needed card appears for the new step, read what it will do before approving. Steps that touch files, programs or the network are checked against your permission rules.

What success looks like

  • The calculation runs on its input data, or the Agent finishes the work with an allowed step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Agent Checks to let quick calculations reach files or the network.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The python_transform sandbox validator rejected the code for defining a class or using global/nonlocal, importing outside the data-module allowlist, calling open, eval, exec, compile, import, getattr, setattr, globals or locals, or accessing a private attribute.

What this means

  • The pure-transform validator detects forbidden imports, dynamic execution, private attributes or state-changing constructs outside its supported sandbox. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The pure-transform validator detects forbidden imports, dynamic execution, private attributes or state-changing constructs outside its supported sandbox.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the rejected AST construct against the pure-transform interface; separate computation from external effects rather than disguising the same access.

How to fix it

  • Limit the transform to pure functions over its inputs and the allowlisted modules (collections, csv, datetime, decimal, fractions, functools, html, itertools, json, math, operator, re, statistics, textwrap); see execution/python.py _assess_transform_sandbox. Use python_action or a Files/Shell capability for I/O, and keep execution.transform_sandbox enabled.
  • Use the advertised pure transform interface or a separately authorized supported capability for external effects. Do not disable the transform sandbox.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The transform uses only supported pure operations and passes the same sandbox check.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the guard as a routine remedy.
  • Do not substitute a different timeout, permission or model setting for this control.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
